title: 114. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Reverse Percentage Problems
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the original value when the final value after a percentage increase is known.
questions.question: After a \(20\%\) increase, a price becomes \(240\text{ yuan}\). What was the original price?
questions.explanation: Let the original price be \(x\). A \(20\%\) increase means the final price is \(1.20x\). Since \(1.20x=240\), we have \(x=\frac{240}{1.20}=200\). Therefore, the original price was \(200\text{ yuan}\). Option B comes from subtracting \(20\%\) of \(240\), which is a common reverse-percentage error.
questions.hint: Express the final amount as a multiple of the original amount.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the original value when the final value after a percentage decrease is known.
questions.question: After a \(25\%\) decrease, a price becomes \(150\text{ yuan}\). What was the original price?
questions.explanation: Let the original price be \(x\). A \(25\%\) decrease means the final price is \(0.75x\). Since \(0.75x=150\), we have \(x=\frac{150}{0.75}=200\). Therefore, the original price was \(200\text{ yuan}\). Option B incorrectly adds \(25\%\) of \(150\) to \(150\).
questions.hint: Decide which fraction of the original amount remains after the change.

questions.concept: Reverse Percentage Increase with Larger Percentage
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the original value when the final value after a \(40\%\) increase is given.
questions.question: After a \(40\%\) increase, a value becomes \(560\). What was the original value?
questions.explanation: Let the original value be \(x\). A \(40\%\) increase gives \(1.40x=560\). Thus \(x=\frac{560}{1.40}=400\). The original value was \(400\). Option A incorrectly finds \(60\%\) of \(560\), which is not the reverse of a \(40\%\) increase.
questions.hint: Work backward through the changes in their reverse order.

questions.concept: Reverse Percentage Decrease with Larger Percentage
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the original value when the final value after a \(30\%\) decrease is given.
questions.question: After a \(30\%\) decrease, a value becomes \(210\). What was the original value?
questions.explanation: Let the original value be \(x\). A \(30\%\) decrease gives \(0.70x=210\). Thus \(x=\frac{210}{0.70}=300\). The original value was \(300\). Option A incorrectly adds \(30\%\) of \(210\) to \(210\).
questions.hint: Express the final amount as a multiple of the original amount.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the original price when the discounted price and discount rate are known.
questions.question: A shirt is sold at a \(15\%\) discount for \(340\text{ yuan}\). What was the original price?
questions.explanation: A \(15\%\) discount means the selling price is \(85\%\) of the original price. Let the original price be \(x\). Then \(0.85x=340\), so \(x=\frac{340}{0.85}=400\). The original price was \(400\text{ yuan}\). Option A incorrectly adds \(15\%\) of \(340\) to \(340\).
questions.hint: Decide which fraction of the original amount remains after the change.

questions.learningObjective: Find the original number when the final number after a \(12\%\) increase is known.
questions.question: After a \(12\%\) increase, a number becomes \(448\). What was the original number?
questions.explanation: Let the original number be \(x\). A \(12\%\) increase gives \(1.12x=448\). Thus \(x=\frac{448}{1.12}=400\). The original number was \(400\). Option B incorrectly subtracts \(12\%\) of \(448\) from \(448\).
questions.hint: Work backward through the changes in their reverse order.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the original mass when the final mass after a \(5\%\) decrease is given.
questions.question: After a \(5\%\) decrease, a mass becomes \(190\text{ kg}\). What was the original mass?
questions.explanation: Let the original mass be \(x\). A \(5\%\) decrease gives \(0.95x=190\). Thus \(x=\frac{190}{0.95}=200\). The original mass was \(200\text{ kg}\). Option B incorrectly adds \(5\%\) of \(190\) to \(190\).
questions.hint: Express the final amount as a multiple of the original amount.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the original population when the final population after a \(60\%\) increase is known.
questions.question: After a \(60\%\) increase, a population becomes \(8{,}000\). What was the original population?
questions.explanation: Let the original population be \(x\). A \(60\%\) increase gives \(1.60x=8{,}000\). Thus \(x=\frac{8{,}000}{1.60}=5{,}000\). The original population was \(5{,}000\). Option B incorrectly takes \(40\%\) of \(8{,}000\), which is not the reverse of a \(60\%\) increase.
questions.hint: Express the final amount as a multiple of the original amount.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the original value when the final value after two successive percentage increases is known.
questions.question: After a \(15\%\) increase and then a \(20\%\) increase, a value becomes \(345\). What was the original value?
questions.explanation: Let the original value be \(x\). The two increases give multipliers \(1.15\) and \(1.20\), so the final value is \(x(1.15)(1.20)=1.38x\). Since \(1.38x=345\), we have \(x=\frac{345}{1.38}=250\). The original value was \(250\). Option B incorrectly subtracts \(35\%\) from \(345\), which ignores that the two percentage increases apply successively.
questions.hint: Work backward through the changes in their reverse order.

questions.concept: Reverse Successive Percentage Decrease and Increase
questions.learningObjective: Determine the original value when a percentage decrease and a percentage increase are applied successively.
questions.question: After a \(10\%\) decrease and then a \(10\%\) increase, a value becomes \(198\). What was the original value?
questions.explanation: Let the original value be \(x\). The two changes give multipliers \(0.90\) and \(1.10\), so the final value is \(x(0.90)(1.10)=0.99x\). Since \(0.99x=198\), we have \(x=\frac{198}{0.99}=200\). The original value was \(200\). Option A incorrectly assumes the \(10\%\) decrease and \(10\%\) increase cancel completely, so the original value would equal the final value.
questions.hint: Express the final amount as a multiple of the original amount.
